title: Geometry of a blowup at a regular surface point
statement: Let $X$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], with Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $p\in X$ be a closed point such that $\dim\mathcal O_{X,p}=2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $b:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] of the reduced closed point. Then $X'$ is integral, regular and Noetherian. The morphism $b$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and is an isomorphism over $X\setminus\{p\}$. For every closed point $q\in X'$ with $b(q)=p$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{X',q}$ has dimension $2$.

source.place: Tags 0AGR (resolve-lemma-blowup-regular) and 0AGQ (resolve-lemma-blowup), with the closed exceptional point dimension calculation in the proof of 0AGR. Global geometric form of these local statements: localize at the closed center, and use that the blowup is an isomorphism away from its center. Integrality, Noetherianity and properness are included; no cohomology assertion is made.

proof.text: The reduced point ideal $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. An affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\ni p$ with $R$ Noetherian exists [pqf-def-locnoeth]; there $\mathcal I$ is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ ($p$ closed), finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; elsewhere it is the unit ideal. These generators give finite free surjections [pqf-def-coherent]. It is nonzero: otherwise the affine stalk $R_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,p}$ would be a field, of dimension $0$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], not $2$. Thus [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] makes $b$ proper; proper includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X'$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme); properties.tex Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian); algebra.tex Noetherian definition; Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6).

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus\{p\}$. The generic stalk of integral $X$ is a field [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], so $p$ is not generic and $U$ is nonempty; its affine rings are domains [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The base is qcqs [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], and its open $U$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier] makes $b^{-1}U$ scheme-theoretically dense, i.e. $\mathcal O_{X'}\to j_*\mathcal O_{b^{-1}U}$ is injective [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $b^{-1}U\cong U$. Its inclusion $j$ is quasi-compact: for affine $W\subseteq X'$, the open $W\cap b^{-1}U$ of the Noetherian $X'$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sfb-schematic-integral-open-criterion] to obtain integrality of $X'$.

source.place: Tags 02NS (properness), 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor: the center pulls back to an effective Cartier divisor, so its complement is scheme-theoretically dense) and the blowup-complement isomorphism; integrality from that density instead of Tag 02ND.

proof.text: Set $A=\mathcal O_{X,p}$, regular local of dimension $2$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The canonical $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is flat and locally $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]; hence $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}=\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak m_A$. Flat blowup comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map, thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] identifies $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m_A}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_X X'$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so the blowup map of $Y$ is the first projection.

For each $q$ over $p$, [lem-sfb-local-spectrum-base-change-stalks] gives a unique lift $\widetilde q\in Y$ and $\mathcal O_{X',q}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,\widetilde q}$. By [lem-sfb-local-surface-maximal-blowup-geometry], $Y$ is regular, so these rings are regular local. Off $p$ the complement isomorphism identifies stalks with those of $X$. Together with Noetherianity this proves regularity [def-weil-regular-scheme]. If $q$ is closed, its lift is closed in $Y$ and lies over $\mathfrak m_A$, hence is closed in the exceptional fibre. The same local surface lemma gives dimension $2$ there; the ring isomorphism preserves prime chains [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], giving dimension $2$ at $q$.
